terminals.name: gcd(x,y)
terminals.description: gcd(x,y) returns the greatest common divisor of x and y. gcd(x,y) is the largest divisor common to x and y. Functions 2920 ni.com To compute gcd(x,y), consider the prime factorizations of x and y: x = Πi piai y = Πi pibi where pi are all the prime factors of x and y. If pi does not occur in a factorization, the corresponding exponent is 0. gcd(x,y) then is given by: gcd(x,y) = Πi pimin(ai , bi) For example, the prime factorizations of 12 and 30 are given by: 12 = 2² × 31 × 50 30 = 21 × 31 × 51 s

Wire data to the x or y input to determine the polymorphic instance to use or manually select the instance. • Point in Polygon (Scalar) VI • Point in Polygon (Array) VI Point in Polygon (Scalar) VI Point in Polygon (Scalar) VI Verifies whether a point is inside a polygon. Wire data to the x or y input to determine the polymorphic instance to use or manually select the instance. Functions © National Instruments 3995

terminals.name: Polygon X
terminals.description: Polygon X specifies the x-coordinates of the vertices of the polygon. The length of Polygon X must be greater than or equal to 3.

terminals.name: Polygon Y
terminals.description: Polygon Y specifies the y-coordinates of the vertices of the polygon. The length of Polygon Y must equal the length of Polygon X.

terminals.name: tolerance
terminals.description: tolerance controls the accuracy of verifying whether a point lies on the boundary. The default is 1E–9. If tolerance is less than 0, the VI sets tolerance to 1E–9.

terminals.name: position
terminals.description: position specifies the position of the given point relative to the polygon. 0 Inside—The given point is inside the polygon. 1 On Boundary—The given point is on the boundary of the polygon. 2 Outside—The given point is outside the polygon.

terminals.name: error
terminals.description: error returns any error or warning from the VI. You can wire error to the Error Cluster From Error Code VI to convert the error code or warning into an error cluster. entries.name: Polygon Centroid
entries.description: Computes the centroid of a polygon. If either input contains NaN or Inf, the VI returns NaN to Centroid X and Centroid Y, and it also returns an error. If the polygon degenerates to a line, the VI returns NaN to Centroid X and Centroid Y without an error.

terminals.name: Centroid X
terminals.description: Centroid X returns the x-coordinate of the centroid.

terminals.name: Centroid Y
terminals.description: Functions 3998 ni.com Centroid Y returns the y-coordinate of the centroid.

terminals.name: error
terminals.description: error returns any error or warning from the VI. You can wire error to the Error Cluster From Error Code VI to convert the error code or warning into an error cluster. The centroid of a polygon is the arithmetic mean of all vertices in the polygon. Any line through the centroid divides the polygon with equal area.

entries.name: Delaunay Triangulation
entries.description: Computes the Delaunay triangulation of the specified points in the plane.

terminals.name: Triangles
terminals.description: Triangles returns an n-by-3 array, where n equals the number of triangles in the Delaunay triangulation. Each row of Triangles represents a triangle of the Delaunay triangulation, using the indexes of the input points (X, Y).

terminals.name: error
terminals.description: error returns any error or warning from the VI. You can wire error to the Error Cluster From Error Code VI to convert the error code or warning into an error cluster. Functions

entries.name: Voronoi Diagram
entries.description: Computes the Voronoi diagram of specified points in a plane.

terminals.name: Voronoi X
terminals.description: Voronoi X returns the x-coordinates of Voronoi points.

terminals.name: Voronoi Y
terminals.description: Voronoi Y returns the y-coordinates of Voronoi points.

terminals.name: Voronoi Edges
terminals.description: Functions 4000 ni.com Voronoi Edges returns an n-by-2 array. n represents the number of edges in the Voronoi diagram. Each row of Voronoi Edges represents an edge of the Voronoi diagram that uses the indexes of Voronoi points.

terminals.name: error
terminals.description: error returns any error or warning from the VI. You can wire error to the Error Cluster From Error Code VI to convert the error code or warning into an error cluster. For n given points in the plane, the Voronoi diagram divides the plane into n Voronoi cells. Each given point belongs to one Voronoi cell. The point in a Voronoi cell is closer to the corresponding given point than to any of the other given points. The following illustration shows an example of a Voronoi diagram of 8 given points.

entries.name: Convex Hull
entries.description: Computes the vertices of a convex polygon, which are the set of points that make up the polygon that contains all the points. Functions © National Instruments 4001

terminals.name: Convex Hull
terminals.description: Convex Hull returns the indexes of the points that compose the convex hull. The first element in Convex Hull is the same as the last element so that the first and last elements form a closed convex hull.

terminals.name: error
terminals.description: error returns any error or warning from the VI. You can wire error to the Error Cluster From Error Code VI to convert the error code or warning into an error cluster. The convex hull of a finite set of points is the smallest convex set that contains all points. In the following illustration, the convex hull is the line that connects the points.

entries.name: Convex Polygon Intersection
entries.description: Computes the intersection of two convex polygons. If two polygons do not intersect, the VI returns empty arrays to Intersection X and Functions 4002 ni.com Intersection Y with no error.

terminals.name: X 1
terminals.description: X 1 specifies the x-coordinates of the vertices of the first polygon. The length of X 1 must be greater than or equal to 3.

terminals.name: Y 1
terminals.description: Y 1 specifies the y-coordinates of the vertices of the first polygon. The length of Y 1 must be equal to X 1.

terminals.name: X 2
terminals.description: X 2 specifies the x-coordinates of the vertices of the second polygon. The length of X 2 must be greater than or equal to 3.

terminals.name: Y 2
terminals.description: Y 2 specifies the y-coordinates of the vertices of the second polygon. The length of Y 2 must be equal to X 2.

terminals.name: Intersection X
terminals.description: Intersection X returns the x-coordinates of the vertices of the intersection polygon.

terminals.name: Intersection Y
terminals.description: Intersection Y returns the y-coordinates of the vertices of the intersection polygon.

entries.name: Add Polynomials
entries.description: Adds two polynomials P(x) and Q(x). The data types you wire to the P(x) and Q(x) inputs determine the polymorphic instance to use. Functions © National Instruments 4007 • Add Polynomials (DBL) VI • Add Polynomials (CDB) VI Add Polynomials (DBL) VI Add Polynomials (DBL) VI Adds two polynomials P(x) and Q(x). The data types you wire to the P(x) and Q(x) inputs determine the polymorphic instance to use.

terminals.name: P(x)
terminals.description: P(x) contains the real polynomial coefficients in ascending order of power.

terminals.name: Q(x)
terminals.description: Q(x) contains the real polynomial coefficients in ascending order of power.

terminals.name: threshold
terminals.description: threshold specifies the level at which the VI removes from P(x)+Q(x) the trailing elements whose absolute values or relative values are less than or equal to threshold. If all the elements in P(x)+Q(x) are less than or equal to threshold, P(x)+Q(x) returns a one- element array.

terminals.name: threshold type
terminals.description: threshold type specifies how the VI removes the trailing elements from P(x)+Q(x). If threshold type is Absolute Value, the VI removes the trailing elements from P(x)+Q(x) whose absolute values are less than or equal to threshold. If threshold type is Relative Value, the VI removes the trailing elements from P(x)+Q(x) whose absolute values are less than or equal to threshold * |x|, where x is the coefficient which has the maximum absolute value in resulting polynomial. Functions 4008 ni.com 0 Abs

terminals.description: P(x)+Q(x) returns the real coefficients for the sum polynomial in ascending order of power.

entries.name: Partial Fraction Expansion
entries.description: Calculates the partial fraction expansion of a polynomial using the Heaviside cover-up method.

terminals.name: Numerator
terminals.description: Numerator contains the rational polynomial coefficients, in ascending order of power, for the numerator polynomial.

terminals.name: Denominator
terminals.description: Denominator contains the rational polynomial coefficients, in ascending order of power, for the denominator polynomial.

terminals.name: tolerance
terminals.description: tolerance defines a level for multiplicity.

terminals.name: option
terminals.description: option specifies how the VI handles the co-factors of Numerator and Denominator. If option is Cancel Co-factors, this VI performs polynomial GCD of Numerator and Denominator first. If option is Reserve Co-factors, this VI keeps Denominator unchanged. 0 Cancel Co-factors 1 Reserve Co-factors (default)

terminals.name: Multiplicity
terminals.description: Functions 4060 ni.com Multiplicity returns the number of times each root in Poles occurs. Multiplicity occurs when the difference between two elements in Poles is less than tolerance.

terminals.name: Polynomial
terminals.description: Polynomial returns the coefficients, in ascending order of power, for the quotient polynomial that results from the division of Numerator by Denominator.

terminals.name: Poles
terminals.description: Poles returns the unique roots of Denominator. The roots of Denominator result from removing all common factors between Numerator and Denominator.

terminals.name: Residues
terminals.description: Residues returns the numerators of the partial fractions that result for each pole.

terminals.name: error
terminals.description: error returns any error or warning from the VI. You can wire error to the Error Cluster From Error Code VI to convert the error code or warning into an error cluster.

entries.name: Create Polynomial From PFE

terminals.name: Multiplicity
